permitting_source.title: ACC Data Center/Large Load Workshop Highlights (Docket E-00000A-25-0069)
permitting_source.shows: The ACC is reviewing large-load and data-center service (universal large-load tariff plus ESAs, bring-your-own-power) while stating a pro-growth posture. No moratorium.
permitting_source.quote: This Commission wants to continue to encourage growth and help spur economic development.
permitting_source.why: A pro-growth regulator with an open large-load cost-allocation docket and pending tariff and BYO-power policy is consistent with Neutral. The tax-incentive restriction in the owner note is not covered by this source.

btm_source.title: APS Rate Rider E-56: Partial Requirements Service (A.C.C. No. 6212)
btm_source.publisher: Arizona Public Service Company (ACC Decision No. 79293)
btm_source.shows: ACC-approved standard rider for customers that serve part of their load from on-site generation of 100 kW or more, with supplemental, back-up and maintenance power.
btm_source.quote: applicable to retail Customers who obtain any part of their electric requirements from on-site generation equipment with a continuous nameplate rating of 100 kW or greater
btm_source.why: Shows on-site self-generation at large-customer scale is a routine tariffed service. It does not address third-party ownership or co-location sales, and Direct Access customers are excluded.

permitting_source.title: Large Load Integration (Batch Zero)
permitting_source.shows: Large-load interconnection in ERCOT runs through an ISO process (Batch Zero under PGRR145) for load facilities of 75 MW or greater, with TSP/DSP submissions and ERCOT classification; no state siting certificate is involved.
permitting_source.quote: load facility of 75 MW or greater through the Batch Zero process
permitting_source.why: Confirms the gating step for a large load is ERCOT's interconnection process, not a state siting review (consistent with Permissive), but Batch Zero plus SB 6's 75 MW standards ($100,000+ study fee, site control, financial commitment) add friction that did not exist before 2025.

btm_source.title: SB 6 (89th Legislature, enrolled) - planning for, interconnection and operation of, and costs related to large loads
btm_source.shows: New Sec. 39.169 requires notice to ERCOT, an ERCOT study and PUC approval/denial/conditions within 60 days for a net metering (co-location) arrangement between an existing stand-alone generator and a new large load; inaction is deemed approval. Sec. 37.0561 requires disclosure of on-site backup generation, which ERCOT may direct to deploy in emergencies.
btm_source.quote: shall approve, deny, or impose reasonable conditions
btm_source.why: Co-location with EXISTING generation now needs ERCOT study and PUC review (deemed approved if no action), and backup generation can be called in emergencies; new-build on-site generation is not restricted. Still broadly Permissive, but with a review step that should be noted.

permitting_source.title: NRS 360.754, Partial abatement of certain taxes imposed on new or expanded data center
permitting_source.shows: Nevada statute directs the Office of Economic Development to approve tax abatements for new or expanded data centers that meet its criteria (effective through 2056), a state posture that encourages DC siting.
permitting_source.quote: A person who intends to locate or expand a data center in this State may apply to the Office of Economic Development pursuant to this section for a partial abatement
permitting_source.why: Shows a pro-data-center state framework (incentives, no DC-specific siting restriction found), consistent with Permissive, but it is an incentive statute, not a permitting rule.

btm_source.title: NRS Chapter 704B (Providers of New Electric Resources), NRS 704B.080 and 704B.310
btm_source.shows: Customers with average annual load of 1 MW or more may buy from an alternative provider of new electric resources, but only on a January filing window, 280 days' notice and a PUCN public-interest finding that weighs costs to remaining customers and reliability.
btm_source.quote: Has an average annual load of 1 megawatt or more in the service territory of an electric utility
btm_source.why: A statutory path off utility supply exists for large customers (supports Permissive), but it is gated by PUCN approval, annual caps and cost tests, which reads closer to Restricted. Addresses third-party supply, not purely on-site self-generation.

markets.tariff_note: No qualifying large-load tariff sourced. permitting_source.title: HB 3546 (2025), Oregon Legislature measure overview (Chapter 323, 2025 Laws)
permitting_source.shows: Enacted law directs the PUC to create a separate service class for large energy use facilities, allocate their costs to them and require contracts, protecting other customers.
permitting_source.quote: Directs the Public Utility Commission to provide for a classification of service for large energy use facilities.
permitting_source.why: A special DC rate class and contract requirement, without a siting moratorium, is consistent with Neutral, but it is a rate measure, not a permitting rule.

btm_source.title: ORS 758.450, Allocated (exclusive) service territories
btm_source.shows: Once territory is allocated, no other person may provide utility service in it; exceptions are only for very small providers and solar/wind providers, plus third-party financing of a customer's own resources.
btm_source.quote: no other person shall offer, construct or extend utility service in or into an allocated territory
btm_source.why: Exclusive territories bar third-party sale of gas-fired or other non-solar/wind supply to a data center, while self-supply and solar/wind are allowed; matches Restricted.

permitting_source.title: Joint Statement of PSC Staff and Georgia Power re Large Load Contract (Docket 44280, Doc. 228126)
permitting_source.shows: Under the PSC's 2025 Large Load Contract Review Process Orders, Georgia Power contracts with customers above 100 MW (predominantly data centers) are reviewed to keep costs off other customers. Staff has cleared six prior contracts.
permitting_source.quote: Large Load Contract Review Process Orders
permitting_source.why: Shows a cost-protection contract review rather than a siting barrier, and large-load contracts are moving through it. That is consistent with Permissive, but the source is about rates and contracts, not siting or permitting.

btm_source.title: Initial Decision, Sawnee EMC v. Georgia Power Co., Docket 43899 (Territorial Electric Service Act)
btm_source.shows: Under the Territorial Act, retail service is reserved to assigned electric suppliers. New single-metered premises of 900 kW or more outside municipal limits may choose among electric suppliers (O.C.G.A. s.46-3-8(a)).
btm_source.quote: O.C.G.A.§46-3-8(a) permits any electric supplier to serve one or more new premises
btm_source.why: Large new loads get a one-time choice among utilities and EMCs, but there is no route for a non-utility third party to sell retail power. That leans Restricted for third-party co-location, while self-owned generation is not addressed. The 2015 Solar Power Free-Market Financing Act (limited third-party solar) could not be fetched from legis.ga.gov.

permitting_source.shows: The CEC licenses all thermal plants of 50 MW or more. Projects of 100 MW or less may seek an exemption only on a showing of no environmental or reliability impacts. Data-center backup-generator fleets have needed SPPEs (e.g., Santa Clara dockets).
permitting_source.quote: licenses thermal power plants 50 megawatts or greater
permitting_source.why: State-level licensing under the Warren-Alquist Act, with a CEQA-equivalent review, applies to on-site thermal generation at data-center scale. That is heavy state siting review and supports Restrictive.

btm_source.publisher: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (CPUC-filed tariff)

btm_source.quote: This schedule is applicable to customers that have Customer Generation Departing Load
btm_source.why: Self-generation is allowed but carries mandatory departing-load charges. Together with the PU Code s.218 limit of serving at most two adjacent parties (official text not retrievable, leginfo returned 403), this fits Restricted, not Prohibitive.

permitting_source.title: Ohio Revised Code 4906.10, Power Siting Board certificate decision
permitting_source.publisher: Ohio Legislative Service Commission (Ohio Revised Code)
permitting_source.shows: As amended by HB 15, the Power Siting Board must decide a generation/transmission certificate within 150 days of a complete application, or the application is deemed approved.

btm_source.title: Ohio Adm.Code 4901:1-10-37, Mercantile customer self-power systems
btm_source.publisher: Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (Ohio Administrative Code)
btm_source.shows: PUCO rule implementing HB 15 (ORC 4928.73): utilities may not block mercantile customer self-power systems (customer- or third-party-owned BTM generation on owned or adjacent property, shareable by several customers).
btm_source.quote: An EDU cannot disallow mercantile customer self-power systems from providing electric generation service
btm_source.why: Statute plus rule expressly authorise third-party-owned behind-the-meter generation for large customers, which is Permissive.

btm_source.shows: Enacts Utah Code 54-26 creating alternative processes for serving large-load customers, including service from large-scale generation providers and a framework for closed private generation systems, partly exempt from rate regulation.
btm_source.quote: establishes a framework for closed private generation systems and connected generation systems
btm_source.why: Enrolled bill creates an explicit path for large loads to be served by non-utility / private generation, consistent with Permissive. (Fetched the enrolled text; the bill status page did not render the governor's action.)

permitting_source.title: CS/CS/SB 484 (2026, enrolled): An act relating to data centers, Ch. 2026-65, Laws of Florida
permitting_source.shows: Approved 2026-05-07, effective 2026-07-01. Codifies local planning and land-use authority over large-load customers, denies them substation-siting preemption, and restricts consumptive water-use permits for large-scale data centers (hearing required; reclaimed water). Also mandates large-load tariff cost protections.
permitting_source.quote: Local governments shall maintain the authority to exercise the powers and responsibilities for comprehensive planning and land development regulation granted by law with respect to large load customers
permitting_source.why: Codified local control plus DC-specific water-permit conditions and hearings add friction beyond Permissive. Florida is not under a moratorium, so Neutral (not Restrictive) fits best.

btm_source.title: Order No. PSC-2018-0251-DS-EQ, Declaratory Statement (Sunrun solar equipment lease), Docket 20170273-EQ
btm_source.shows: Applying s.366.02(1), F.S. and Rule 25-6.065, F.A.C., the PSC allows third-party leases of on-site renewable systems only where no retail sale of electricity from the third party occurs.
btm_source.quote: under terms and conditions that do not include the retail purchase of electricity from the third party
btm_source.why: Florida treats anyone supplying electricity to the public as a regulated utility, so third-party retail sales (PPA or co-located seller) are barred and only customer-owned or leased equipment is allowed. A third-party-sale ban matches Restricted. Customer-owned self-generation remains permitted.

permitting_source.title: Lawmakers Mark Signing of Landmark Data Center Protections
permitting_source.shows: HB 2992 (Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act, effective 1 July 2026) protects existing customers from large-load costs and requires developers to notify neighbours, county commissioners and the OCC within 60 days of acquiring land; no state siting approval or moratorium.
permitting_source.quote: notify adjoining landowners, county commissioners, and the Corporation Commission within 60 days of acquiring land
permitting_source.why: The state's DC law imposes cost protection and a notice duty only, no siting review; consistent with Permissive. (Separate SB 259 adds a groundwater permit.)

btm_source.title: HB 2992 committee substitute (Data Center Consumer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026)
btm_source.shows: Defines 'large load customer' (new data centers etc. adding >=75 MW) and expressly excludes entities that build their own generation for behind-the-meter projects from the large-load regime.
btm_source.quote: or those entities that build generation for behind-the-meter projects
btm_source.why: Carving BTM projects out of the large-load rules supports Permissive, but this is a committee-substitute text, not the enrolled act (enrolled text not fetched), and it does not itself authorise third-party sales.

permitting_source.title: SB 94 (2026) Siting of data centers; site assessment; high energy use facility - Acts of Assembly Chapter 568
permitting_source.shows: Approved by the Governor as Chapter 568 (effective 7/1/2026): before any rezoning, special exception or special use permit for a new high energy use facility, a locality must require a site assessment of sound impacts on homes and schools within 500 feet, and may require assessment of water, agricultural, park, historic and forest impacts.
permitting_source.quote: a locality shall require that an applicant perform and submit a site assessment to examine the sound profile of the HEUF
permitting_source.why: A state-mandated, data-center-specific pre-approval study requirement layered on local discretionary approval (and expressly preserving local zoning authority) fits Restrictive. Content read through the LIS public API that backs this page (summary as passed + history).

btm_source.title: SB 253 (2026) Electric utilities; pilot programs...; large-load cost allocation; standby tariff - Acts of Assembly Chapter 1124
btm_source.shows: Approved as Chapter 1124 (effective 7/1/2026; identical HB 1393 = Ch. 1123): Dominion must propose allocating certain capacity-procurement and distribution costs to the 25 MW+ / 75%+ load-factor class, and must propose a revised supplementary, maintenance or standby service tariff for customers with power plants (effective 1/1/2028) that includes protections against stranded cost risks.
btm_source.quote: a proposal to revise its tariff for supplementary, maintenance, or standby service for customers with power plants
btm_source.why: On-site generation is allowed but its standby terms are being re-set with stranded-cost protections, and large loads carry more of the cost, consistent with Restricted (cost-conditioned, not barred). OWNER NOTE CORRECTION: 2026 SB 484 is NOT an energy bill. It is 'Department of General Services; independent agency; evaluation', and it was tabled in House Appropriations 3/9/2026. The 'effective July 1 2026, large-load cost' provision matches SB 253 / HB 1393 (Ch. 1124 / 1123). It directs Dominion to PROPOSE the allocation to the SCC, which is not a statutory 'full cost of service' mandate. (Florida 2026 SB 484 is the bill with 'full cost' large-load tariff language.)

permitting_source.title: Wyoming Statutes Title 35, W.S. 35-12-106 (Industrial Development Information and Siting Act)
permitting_source.shows: No one may begin construction of a covered industrial 'facility' without an Industrial Siting Council permit.
permitting_source.quote: No person shall commence to construct a facility, as defined in this chapter, in this state without first obtaining a permit for that facility from the council.
permitting_source.why: Confirms a single state Industrial Siting Council permit for large projects, a defined one-stop process consistent with a business-friendly regime. The statute itself does not show 'easy' (thresholds are in 35-12-102, not extracted).

btm_source.title: Wyoming Statutes Title 37, W.S. 37-1-101(a)(vi)(H)(VI) - 'Public utility' exemptions
btm_source.shows: The public utility chapter does not apply to generation of electricity by a person for its own sole use or its tenants' use and not for sale to others.
btm_source.quote: for the sole use of a producer or other person, or for the use of tenants of a producer or other person and not for sale to others
btm_source.why: Self-generation for a large load's own use is outside PSC regulation, which supports Permissive for owner-operated BTM. Third-party sale to the load would still make the seller a public utility, so third-party BTM is more constrained than the Permissive label implies.

permitting_source.title: AQB 26-57(P): Yucca Growth Infrastructure, LLC - YGI Microgrid (Project Jupiter)
permitting_source.publisher: New Mexico Environment Department, Office of Public Facilitation
permitting_source.shows: The state's main permitting step for the Project Jupiter data-center microgrid is an ordinary NMED air construction permit (NSR), now in a contested public hearing with motions pending and a 23 Nov 2026 decision deadline.
permitting_source.quote: AQB 26-57(P): Yucca Growth Infrastructure, LLC - YGI Microgrid (Project Jupiter)
permitting_source.why: No DC-specific state siting regime (only the generic air permit), which fits Permissive, but the docket shows a heavily contested, litigated hearing, so permitting friction in practice is higher than 'streamlined'. Latest filing listed 2026-10-13; no final decision yet.

btm_source.title: Fiscal Impact Report, SB 235/SCONCS (Microgrid Oversight Act), 2026 Regular Session
btm_source.shows: States that privately developed microgrids (including large-load self-supply) need no PRC certificate, only local zoning and a building permit; SB 235, which would have put them under PRC oversight, passed the Senate but did not pass the House (per secondary sources).
btm_source.quote: Microgrids do not require a certificate of convenience and necessity from PRC but do require zoning approval of the local jurisdiction and a building permit.
btm_source.why: Self-supplied/off-grid generation for a large load sits outside PRC certification, consistent with Permissive. Watch item: a renewed microgrid-oversight bill would tighten this.

permitting_source.title: H.3309, South Carolina Energy Security Act (Act No. 41 of 2025)
permitting_source.shows: Enacted act instructs all state agencies to expedite review of energy infrastructure permit applications and favours siting in existing energy corridors and brownfield generation sites.
permitting_source.quote: All agencies are instructed to give expedited review of applications for energy infrastructure projects
permitting_source.why: A statutory expedited-review directive for energy infrastructure supports a Permissive tier for the power supply side.

btm_source.title: H.3309, South Carolina Energy Security Act (Act No. 41 of 2025), Section 32 adding S.C. Code 58-41-50
btm_source.shows: Co-located generation or storage for nonresidential customers over 25 MW is encouraged, but through agreements the electrical utility files for Public Service Commission consideration.
btm_source.quote: An electrical utility may file a proposed agreement regarding co-located resources between the utility and a customer or multiple customers with an electric load in excess of 25 megawatts
btm_source.why: The state encourages co-location (pro-Permissive) but routes it through the incumbent utility and PSC approval rather than letting customers or third parties self-supply freely. This reads closer to Restricted; worth an owner review.

permitting_source.title: SB25-280 Colorado Data Center Development and Grid Modernization Act

permitting_source.quote: Colorado Data Center Development and Grid Modernization Act
permitting_source.why: Shows Colorado has no enacted statewide data-center framework, so siting stays with local land-use authority. It neither confirms streamlined permitting nor shows a restriction. Weak fit; a stronger Colorado source was not found within budget.

permitting_source.title: House Bill 911 (2026): New large load and ratepayer protection (new Idaho Code 61-335)
permitting_source.shows: Signed 2026-04-10 (Session Law ch. 335, effective 2026-07-01). A public utility may serve a new load of 50 MW or more only under a PUC-approved service contract, with a no-harm test, full cost of service, financial security, anti-splitting rules, and a review of up to 270 days.
permitting_source.quote: A public utility shall provide service to a new large load only pursuant to a commission-approved service contract.
permitting_source.why: A mandatory case-by-case PUC approval (up to 270 days) for every load of 50 MW or more is a data-center-specific state requirement. Idaho still has no state generation-siting regime or moratorium, so this points to Neutral rather than Permissive.

btm_source.title: Idaho Code 61-332B (Electric Supplier Stabilization Act)
btm_source.shows: Bars an electric supplier from serving a service entrance already connected to another supplier. Under 61-332A, an "electric supplier" is a public utility, cooperative or municipality.
btm_source.quote: No electric supplier shall supply or furnish electric service to any electric service entrance
btm_source.why: Territorial protection applies between utilities, co-ops and municipalities. It does not bar a customer's own on-site generation, which supports Permissive for self-supply. A non-utility third party selling at retail would raise public-utility questions that were not verified here.

large_load_tariff.name: Schedule 20 - Speculative High-Density Load

permitting_source.title: 20 ILCS 605/605-1025: Data center investment
permitting_source.shows: State tax exemptions and credits for data centers investing at least $250M with 20 or more jobs. Recipients must certify carbon neutrality or green-building status within 2 years and use a project labor agreement. New certificates sunset after July 1, 2029.
permitting_source.quote: certifies to the Department that it is carbon neutral or has attained certification under one or more of the following green building standards
permitting_source.why: A pro-development incentive with added conditions (carbon-neutral or green-building certification, labor terms). That fits Neutral, but it is an incentive statute, not a siting or permitting rule.

btm_source.title: 220 ILCS 5/16-102: Definitions ("Alternative retail electric supplier")
btm_source.shows: Excluded from the ARES definition (so no ARES license is needed): a customer using its own cogeneration or self-generation, and a third party that owns, operates or arranges installation of the customer's self-generation (subject to labor provisions). 220 ILCS 5/3-105 also excludes PURPA QFs and ARES from "public utility". Third-party energy sales are possible with ICC ARES certification in this retail-choice state.
btm_source.quote: a retail customer to the extent that customer obtains its electric power and energy from that customer's own cogeneration or self-generation facilities
btm_source.why: The statute expressly carves out self-generation and third-party-owned or operated on-site generation, and retail choice allows licensed third-party supply. That does not fit Restricted. (CEJA emission limits on new fossil units are a generation-permitting matter, not a BTM bar.)

large_load_tariff.name: Large Demand Project Applicant or Customer deposits (GT&C + Rider DE revisions)
large_load_tariff.quote: ComEd's newly approved tariff changes to add deposit protection for ComEd and its existing customers in the event a large demand project is canceled or abandoned
large_load_tariff.note: Order dated 2026-03-19 (confirmed by ComEd compliance filing https://icc.illinois.gov/downloads/public/filing/4/397281.pdf, tariffs effective 2026-03-31); deposits for >=50 MW projects; ICC ordered a follow-on investigation on a separate large-load tariff structure.

permitting_source.title: RCW 80.50.060 - Energy facilities - Application of chapter
permitting_source.shows: Energy facilities above the RCW 80.50.020 thresholds must obtain EFSEC site certification; developers of alternative energy, storage and certain transmission projects may opt into the state process.
permitting_source.quote: No construction or reconstruction of such energy facilities may be undertaken, except as otherwise provided in this chapter, without first obtaining certification
permitting_source.why: Mandatory state certification for large thermal plants, plus an optional state one-stop path for renewables and storage, is a mixed (Neutral) siting posture.

btm_source.title: RCW 80.04.010 - Definitions ('Electrical company')
btm_source.shows: Any person operating an electric plant for hire is a regulated 'electrical company'; the exclusion covers cogeneration solely for the owner's own use or its tenants, or sales to utilities and public agencies, 'but not for sale to others'.
btm_source.quote: solely for the generation of electricity for its own use or the use of its tenants
btm_source.why: Self-supply (cogeneration) is exempt, but a third party selling on-site power to a data center would be a regulated electrical company. That matches Restricted.

large_load_tariff.name: Rate Schedule No. 94 - New Large Load Service
large_load_tariff.quote: APPLICABILITY: To all New Large Loads, as defined by the District's Customer Service Policies.
large_load_tariff.note: Consumer-owned PUD; approved by the Grant PUD Commission (not the UTC). New large loads pay the greater of Mid-C index or Schedule 15 top block +5%.

permitting_source.title: N.D. Cent. Code ch. 49-22 Energy Conversion and Transmission Facility Siting Act
permitting_source.shows: Non-wind generation over 50 MW (wind over 0.5 MW) needs a PSC certificate of site compatibility, which does not preempt local zoning; onsite backup generation is excluded.
permitting_source.quote: may not supersede or preempt any local land use, zoning, or building rules
permitting_source.why: There is a state siting step plus local zoning for larger plants, but onsite backup generation is excluded and there is no data-center-specific restriction. A partial fit with Permissive.

btm_source.title: N.D. Cent. Code ch. 49-03 Electric Utility Franchise
btm_source.shows: Electric public utilities need a PSC certificate and order to extend lines or serve customers outside municipal limits; the chapter protects incumbent utility and cooperative service.
btm_source.quote: nor shall it serve any customer where the place to be served is not located within the corporate limits
btm_source.why: This is a utility franchise/territorial-protection regime (rubric: Restricted-type), but it governs utilities and does not restrict a customer's own on-site generation. It does not confirm Permissive; no primary source on ND self-generation or co-location was found.

large_load_tariff.name: High Density Contracted Demand Response Rate 45 (data centers, >=10 MW, ESA approved by PSC)

permitting_source.title: Docket M-2025-3054271, Interconnection and Tariffs for Large Load Customers
permitting_source.shows: PUC proceeding that adopted (Final Order adopted 30 Apr 2026, entered 12 May 2026) a model tariff for customers at or over 50 MW individually or 100 MW aggregate, governing interconnection terms rather than siting.
permitting_source.quote: INTERCONNECTION AND TARIFFS FOR LARGE LOAD CUSTOMERS
permitting_source.why: Shows a standardised large-load framework (special requirements, no moratorium), consistent with Neutral; it does not address land-use siting, which is local (municipal) in PA.

btm_source.title: Final Order, Interconnection and Tariffs for Large Load Customers, Docket M-2025-3054271
btm_source.shows: The PUC declined to require large loads to bring their own generation; the tentative order only 'entertained' voluntary BYOG/self-supply, and the model tariff adds no BYOG provisions.
btm_source.quote: we will not add provisions to the model tariff at this time related to requiring Large Load Customers to bring their own generation
btm_source.why: Neither encourages nor prohibits on-site/co-located supply; the state rule leaves BYOG voluntary. Restricted rests more on PJM/FERC co-location rules and PA utility-service law, which this order does not address.

large_load_tariff.name: Rate Schedule LP-6 (large load / data center) - 10-yr minimum commitment, minimum demand guarantees, financial protections

permitting_source.shows: Requires every electric public utility to file a BPU tariff for large load data centers (introduced at >=100 MW), with 85% / 10-year take-or-pay guarantees, deposits and a non-duplication showing, to protect other ratepayers.

btm_source.title: Order, In the Matter of the Petition of DCO Energy for a Declaratory Ruling (MTCC on-site generation facility)
btm_source.publisher: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities
btm_source.shows: BPU explains that EDECA (N.J.S.A. 48:3-51) allows on-site generation to sell to an end user only as a narrow exception to the utility's exclusive franchise, limited to the same or contiguous property; off-site sales must use the franchised utility's wires (N.J.S.A. 48:3-77.1).
btm_source.quote: EDECA then grants a limited exception to that exclusive franchise for an on-site generator so long as its customer is within certain proximity requirements
btm_source.why: On-site / co-located supply is allowed but only within a contiguity limit carved out of the utility's exclusive franchise, which matches Restricted. Docket QO20030191.

permitting_source.title: HS 1 for HB 233 (engrossed; signed 2026-08-26; 85 Del. Laws c. 440): large energy use facilities
permitting_source.shows: No large energy use facility (75 MW at 85% load factor, 100 MW instantaneous, or 30 MW for data centers) may begin operations without PSC approval of its Electric Service Agreement.
permitting_source.quote: No person or entity may begin operations as a large energy use facility served by a Commission-regulated electric utility without first obtaining from the Commission the approval of an Electric Service Agreement
permitting_source.why: A state PSC approval gate before operation, with DC-specific community, labor and climate criteria, is heavy state review of large loads, which matches the Restrictive definition. Note: the text fetched is the substitute as released 2026-05-21; the enacted version includes House and Senate amendments (SA 2 reportedly adds a 30 MW data-processing threshold) that were not separately verified. The signing is confirmed by Governor's Legislative Advisory #56.

btm_source.title: House Substitute 1 for HB 233: An Act to Amend Title 26 Relating to Large Energy Use Facilities
btm_source.shows: New in-state generation built by or for a large facility is a positive factor in ESA approval and can exempt the facility from curtailment requirements.
btm_source.quote: It shall be considered a positive factor in evaluating an ESA if a large energy use facility constructs or causes the construction of new generation
btm_source.why: Rewards facility-built new generation, which leans away from Restricted for self-supply. It does not address behind-the-meter configuration or the legality of third-party retail sales, so it neither confirms nor overturns Restricted.

permitting_source.title: MCA 75-20-104 Definitions (Major Facility Siting Act)
permitting_source.shows: The MFSA 'facility' definition covers transmission lines over 69 kV, large pipelines, geothermal and (for one section) 50 MW+ hydro; non-hydro generating plants are not subject to state MFSA certification.
permitting_source.quote: each electric transmission line and associated facilities of a design capacity of more than 69 kilovolts
permitting_source.why: No state siting certificate is required for thermal/wind/solar generation, so generation permitting is light; consistent with Permissive (transmission still needs MFSA).

btm_source.title: MCA 69-8-201 Customer choice
btm_source.shows: Customers with load of 5,000 kW or more that are not on utility supply may buy from other electricity suppliers, and self-generation and cogeneration rights are unaffected.
btm_source.quote: greater than or equal to 5,000 kilowatts
btm_source.why: Large loads can source supply outside the utility and self-generation is preserved: consistent with Permissive.

large_load_tariff.name: Large New Load Tariff Rule (Rule No. 24), new/expanded loads >= 5 MW

permitting_source.title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 70-1012 Power Review Board approval of generation facilities
permitting_source.shows: Any supplier must get Nebraska Power Review Board approval before building or acquiring generation, storage, or transmission over 700 V; privately developed renewables that meet 70-1014.02 are exempt.
permitting_source.quote: electric generation facilities
permitting_source.why: A state approval gate for generation applies (a friction), with an exemption path for private renewables. It does not address data center siting. Only a partial fit with Permissive.

btm_source.title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 70-1014.02 Privately developed renewable energy generation facility; exemption
btm_source.shows: Private renewable facilities can skip Power Review Board approval with notice and conditions, but the statute does not authorize private suppliers to sell electricity at retail in Nebraska.
btm_source.quote: Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize a private electric supplier to sell
btm_source.why: In this all-public-power state, a private developer cannot sell at retail to a data center; only self-supply or supply through the public power district is open. Under the rubric (third-party-sale bans / franchise exclusivity) this is Restricted, not Permissive.

permitting_source.title: House Bill 2014 (2025 RS) - Certified Microgrid Program / high impact data centers
permitting_source.shows: Enacted (effective July 11, 2025): certified microgrid districts and certified high impact data centers are exempt from county and municipal zoning, noise, land-use and building-permit ordinances and approvals (enrolled text, sec. 5B-2-21 as amended).
permitting_source.quote: may not be subject to the following: (1) County or municipal zoning, horticultural, noise, viewshed, lighting, development, or land use ordinances
permitting_source.why: State law preempts local land-use control for certified data centers and microgrid districts, which is a streamlined, pro-siting regime, not Neutral.

btm_source.title: HB 2014 (2025) Enrolled Committee Substitute - microgrid electric service requirements
btm_source.shows: Within a certified microgrid district, an entity generating or distributing electricity to businesses there is not subject to PSC jurisdiction over rates or certificates of convenience and necessity, and an eligible new-load facility is not required to connect to a public utility.
btm_source.quote: Not be subject to the jurisdiction of the Public Service Commission with respect to rates, obtaining a certificate of convenience and necessity
btm_source.why: Expressly authorizes non-utility on-site and microgrid supply to new large loads outside PSC rate and CCN regulation (generation must be used inside the district or sold wholesale). That is a Permissive BTM posture, at least inside certified districts; outside them, default utility franchise rules still apply.

permitting_source.title: SB 98 (2025): Providing a sales tax exemption for the construction or remodeling of a qualified data center in Kansas
permitting_source.shows: Enacted (Signed by Governor) sales tax exemption for qualified data centers with at least $250M investment plus job requirements. No energy or siting conditions are listed.
permitting_source.quote: Providing a sales tax exemption for the construction or remodeling of a qualified data center in Kansas
permitting_source.why: The state is actively recruiting data centers with no added siting conditions. The KCC's 2025-11-06 approval of Evergy's Large Load Power Service plan (>75 MW, kcc.ks.gov/news-11-6-25) was framed around helping Kansas "properly compete" for these loads. Both fit Permissive.

btm_source.title: K.S.A. 66-1,173: Rights and responsibilities of suppliers (Retail Electric Suppliers Act)
btm_source.publisher: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes
btm_source.shows: Each certified retail electric supplier has the exclusive right to serve all electric-consuming facilities in its territory. Under 66-1,170(d), a "retail electric supplier" is any person engaged in furnishing retail electric service.
btm_source.quote: Every retail electric supplier shall have the exclusive right and responsibility to furnish retail electric service to all electric consuming facilities located within its certified territory
btm_source.why: Statutory franchise exclusivity: a third party selling power to a large load would be furnishing retail electric service inside a certified territory. A customer's own on-site generation is not barred, but third-party BTM supply is, which matches the Restricted criteria.

large_load_tariff.name: Large Load Power Service (LLPS) rate plan (with Customer Capacity Rider and Demand Response & Local Generation Rider)
large_load_tariff.quote: Commission approved the Settlement on November 6, 2025.
large_load_tariff.note: Applies to new load or growth >75 MW; 12-year base term plus up to 5-year ramp; take-or-pay minimum; filed 2025-02-11. KCC release: https://www.kcc.ks.gov/news-11-6-25

large_load_tariff.name: Large Load Power Service (LLPS) rate plan
large_load_tariff.quote: approved a unanimous settlement agreement creating a Large Load Power Service (LLPS) rate plan
large_load_tariff.note: Same joint Evergy Kansas Central / Kansas Metro docket (EKME); serves the Kansas City metro side of the state.

permitting_source.title: IURC Order, Cause No. 46097: Indiana Michigan Power Company modifications to Tariff I.P. (large load terms)
permitting_source.shows: Approves a settlement (with Amazon, Google, Microsoft and others) creating large-load terms for loads over 150 MW: long contract terms, minimum billing demand, collateral, and exit fees. Capacity reductions beyond 20% need IURC approval.
permitting_source.quote: I&M's proposed Tariff I.P., as modified by the Settlement Agreement and shown in Settlement Agreement Attachment A, is approved as set forth herein.
permitting_source.why: Shows a settled, published tariff pathway for hyperscale loads (consistent with an accommodating state), with financial protections rather than siting barriers. It is a rate order, not a siting or permitting rule. Indiana Code pages (iga.in.gov) could not be loaded.

btm_source.title: IURC Order, Cause No. 46183: NIPSCO / NIPSCO Generation LLC (GenCo) framework to serve megaload customers
btm_source.shows: The approved settlement lets NIPSCO's generation affiliate compete with other suppliers to build behind-the-meter installations for customers. NIPSCO stays the sole retail electric provider.
btm_source.quote: GenCo may compete with other potential suppliers to construct behind the meter installations for new or existing customers.
btm_source.why: The commission-approved settlement contemplates competitive behind-the-meter installations for large loads, which fits Permissive. The same order keeps NIPSCO as "the sole provider of retail electric service", so third-party retail sales are not opened.

large_load_tariff.name: Tariff I.P. (Industrial Power) large load provisions
large_load_tariff.quote: I&M's proposed Tariff I.P., as modified by the Settlement Agreement and shown in Settlement Agreement Attachment A, is approved as set forth herein.
large_load_tariff.note: Settlement with Amazon, Google, Microsoft, DCC, OUCC, CAC; minimum demand charge, collateral (24x monthly bill), exit terms; >20% capacity reductions need IURC approval.

large_load_tariff.name: GenCo framework to serve 'megaload' (data center) customers
large_load_tariff.quote: Based on the magnitude of potential electric load, NIPSCO refers to these potential customers as "megaload customers."
large_load_tariff.note: Order approving the GenCo settlement (limited declination); a framework, not a tariff schedule. First special contract (Amazon, Data Center Customer #1) decided in Cause No. 46322, order https://www.in.gov/iurc/files/ord_46322_061726.pdf (2026-06-17).

permitting_source.title: Rate Rider EDI (Economic Development Incentive)
permitting_source.publisher: Alabama Power Company (tariff approved by the Alabama Public Service Commission, Docket U-5017)
permitting_source.shows: PSC-approved base-rate incentive for new incremental loads of 1,000 kW or more, with no data-center exclusion.
permitting_source.quote: Incremental metered load of at least one thousand kilowatts (1,000 kW) at a new premises
permitting_source.why: Shows a pro-growth regulatory posture for new large loads, but it is a rate incentive, not a siting or permitting rule. No state-level data-center siting statute or moratorium was found to cite.

btm_source.title: Rate Rider RGB: Supplementary, Back-up, or Maintenance Power
btm_source.publisher: Alabama Power Company (by order of the Alabama Public Service Commission, Informal Docket U-4226)
btm_source.shows: On-site parallel generation is accommodated through a mandatory partial-requirements rider. Large-power rates (LPL, RTP) get firm back-up without the $5.41/kW Capacity Reservation Charge that applies to smaller classes.
btm_source.quote: Required for any customer connected to the Company's system where the customer obtains any portion of its electric requirements from installed on-site, non-emergency electric generating capacity
btm_source.why: Confirms self-generation is allowed with standby service, and the capacity charge does not apply to large-power rates. It says nothing about third-party ownership or sales, so it only partly supports Permissive.

permitting_source.title: Executive Order No. 62: Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers in New York While the State Develops Higher Standards
permitting_source.publisher: Office of the Governor of New York
permitting_source.shows: Directs DEC to hold in abeyance discretionary permit applications for data centers of 50 MW or more until DPS completes a Generic EIS in Case 26-E-0045 (up to about a year).
permitting_source.quote: hold in abeyance all applications for any discretionary permit, approval, license
permitting_source.why: A statewide moratorium on state permits for >=50 MW data centers is the textbook Restrictive case; Neutral understates it until the GEIS is finished and the moratorium lifts. (Local permits are not covered.)

btm_source.title: New York Public Service Law Section 2 (Definitions)
btm_source.shows: Co-generation, alternate energy and small hydro facilities escape regulation as an 'electric corporation' only when they sell to users at or near the project site, and a 'co-generation facility' is capped at 80 MW (120 MW at certain Port Authority sites).
btm_source.quote: distributed solely from one or more of such facilities to users located at or near a project site
btm_source.why: Behind-the-meter supply outside utility regulation is limited to qualifying near-site facilities with a size cap, consistent with Restricted. Note EO 62 says the state wants large loads to 'pay their fair share or supply their own power', so PSC policy may loosen this.

permitting_source.title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 62-110.1 Certificate for construction of generating facility
permitting_source.shows: Any utility or other person needs a Utilities Commission certificate before building generation for public utility service; generation built primarily for the owner's own use needs only a report.
permitting_source.quote: no public utility or other person shall begin the construction of any steam, water, or other facility
permitting_source.why: Merchant/utility generation faces a CPCN, a moderate friction; own-use plants are exempt. Says nothing on data center (load) siting, so it only partly supports Permissive.

btm_source.title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 62-3 Definitions (subdivision 23, public utility)
btm_source.shows: Anyone furnishing electricity to or for the public for compensation is a public utility; exclusions cover generation for one's own use and Article 6B solar leasing only.
btm_source.quote: to or for the public for compensation
btm_source.why: Self-generation is allowed, but a third party selling on-site power to a data center is a public utility (no PPA exclusion; only the limited Article 6B solar lease). Under the rubric's third-party-sale criterion this is Restricted, not Permissive.

btm_source.title: HB 1847 / SB 2128 (114th General Assembly), relative to data centers - Public Chapter 961
btm_source.shows: As amended and signed, a data center (50 MW+ projected peak) may buy energy, capacity or ancillary services from an in-state independent power producer via a direct behind-the-meter interconnection (with utility written approval if it also takes utility service), and must bear its own infrastructure costs.
btm_source.quote: behind the data center's meter
btm_source.why: Statute expressly authorizes behind-the-meter IPP supply to data centers (applies to conduct and contracts on or after July 1, 2026); the only condition is utility written approval when the data center also takes utility service. Note: TVA wholesale contracts with local power companies are a separate constraint not covered by this source (tva.com returned 403).

permitting_source.title: Maryland Public Utilities Article 4-212: Large load customers rate schedules
permitting_source.shows: Requires IOUs and co-ops to file large-load rate schedules by 2026-09-01 for customers of at least 100 MW and over 80% load factor. Required elements include minimum billing demand, long-term commitments, exit fees, collateral and cancellation penalties, and PSC regulations are due by 2026-06-01.
permitting_source.quote: long-term contractual commitments and exit fees
permitting_source.why: A data-center-targeted statutory regime (special DC requirements) supports a stricter tier. It governs rates and terms rather than siting, though. Maryland's CPCN requirement for generation (see btm) is the siting-side friction.

btm_source.title: CPCN (Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity), Maryland Public Service Commission
btm_source.shows: New generating stations need a CPCN. Under PUA 7-207.1, on-site generation is exempt from the full CPCN (still requiring PSC approval) only up to 70 MW with less than 20% exported, or up to 25 MW with at least 10% consumed on site. Emergency generators up to 70 MW that do not export also qualify.
btm_source.quote: the capacity of the generating station does not exceed 70 megawatts
btm_source.why: On-site generation above 70 MW (typical for a hyperscale campus) needs a full CPCN (a separate PSC search result put the average at 388 days versus 60 for exemptions; this page does not state it). Smaller on-site generation still needs PSC approval. That fits Restricted.

large_load_tariff.name: Schedule LL - Large Load Tariff
large_load_tariff.publisher: Potomac Edison filing to Maryland PSC
large_load_tariff.quote: hereby submits for the Maryland Public Service Commission's approval this proposal to create a separate class of large load customers
large_load_tariff.note: 85% minimum demand, collateral, >=10-yr ESA plus ramp, exit after year 7 with 36-month exit fee; filed under PUA 4-212 (Next Generation Energy Act).

permitting_source.title: LPSC B&E Minutes, December 17, 2025: Directive on Commission's Lightning Initiative
permitting_source.shows: Adopted 4-1. Waives the market-based-mechanism (RFP) general order for utility capacity added for a new or expanding load with a signed ESA of at least 15 years and an LED letter. Staff are directed to aim for a Commission vote within 8 months of the application.
permitting_source.quote: with the objective of the Commission being able to vote within 8 months of an application
permitting_source.why: A state fast-track that waives procurement requirements to serve new large loads is a speed-to-market posture, beyond Neutral. LPSC's non-binding large-load guidelines add cost-protection expectations on the utility but no siting barrier.

large_load_tariff.name: Schedule LLHLFPS-L - Large Load, High Load Factor Power Service
large_load_tariff.quote: Customers who contract for not less than 70 MW of firm load with facilities operating with at least an 80% average monthly electric load factor
large_load_tariff.note: Legacy large-load/high-load-factor rate (first revision effective 2024-08-30 under LPSC Order U-36959), not a data-center-specific protection tariff. Separately, LPSC adopted the 'Lightning' directive 2025-12-17 (MBM waivers for qualifying large loads; minutes https://lpsc.louisiana.gov/docs/minutes/Dec_17_2025_Min.pdf); Lewis large-load rulemaking directive was still on the 2026-03-18 agenda. Meta load served via special ESA (U-37425).

permitting_source.title: Act 851 of 2023 (HB 1799): Arkansas Data Centers Act of 2023
permitting_source.shows: Codifies a legislative finding that data centers bring economic value and bars local governments from discriminatory rules against digital-asset mining businesses.
permitting_source.quote: Recognize that data centers create jobs, pay taxes, and provide general economic value to local communities and this state
permitting_source.why: Pro-data-center legislative intent supports Permissive, but the operative protections target crypto mining and still require compliance with local ordinances. It is not a general siting-streamlining law.

btm_source.title: Act 464 of 2019 (SB 145): amending the Arkansas Renewable Energy Development Act of 2001
btm_source.shows: Allows customers to lease on-site net-metering facilities, and lessors are not public utilities, but the lease may not sell energy or capacity per kWh or per kW.
btm_source.quote: A lease shall not permit the sale of electric energy measured in kilowatt hours or electric capacity measured in kilowatts between the lessor and lessee
btm_source.why: Third-party ownership is allowed only as a lease, with no per-kWh sale, which leans Restricted for third-party PPA models. It is limited to net-metering facilities and does not address large non-net-metered self-generation.

permitting_source.title: House Bill 5120 of 2023 (Public Act 233 of 2023)
permitting_source.shows: PA 233 lets the MPSC certify large solar, wind and storage facilities, with zoning exemptions, when local units do not adopt a compatible ordinance or block a compliant project.
permitting_source.quote: authorize MPSC certification for zoning exemptions
permitting_source.why: Supports a permissive generation-permitting posture (state backstop over local zoning), but covers only renewables/storage and local units keep first say; it says nothing on data center (load) siting. Michigan michigan.gov MPSC pages returned 403 so the bill page is used.

btm_source.title: MCL 460.10a (Customer Choice and Electricity Reliability Act, sec. 10a)
btm_source.shows: Protects a customer's right to self-service power (on-site generation without the utility's T&D system, generator may be separately owned) with no exit or transition fees, while capping grid-delivered retail choice at 10%.
btm_source.quote: This act does not prohibit or limit the right of a person to obtain self-service power
btm_source.why: On-site/co-located self-service power is expressly protected and the user is not treated as an electric utility; only grid-delivered choice is capped (10%).

large_load_tariff.name: Rate GPD large-load provisions (100 MW+ customers: 15-yr minimum term, 80% minimum billing demand, exit fee, collateral)
large_load_tariff.quote: today approved Consumers Energy's application to amend the terms and conditions under which it serves data centers
large_load_tariff.note: MPSC release (WebFetch 403; verified by direct fetch). Attorney General sought review of the order.

permitting_source.title: Chapter 239 of the Acts of 2024: An Act Promoting a Clean Energy Grid, Advancing Equity and Protecting Ratepayers
permitting_source.shows: Creates consolidated local and EFSB permits with 12-month decision deadlines and constructive approval, but only for CLEAN energy infrastructure. Small-facility T&D that solely interconnects new fossil generation is excluded from 2026.
permitting_source.quote: If a final decision is not issued within 12 months of the receipt of a complete permit application, a constructive approval permit shall be issued
permitting_source.why: Streamlining helps clean supply. Fossil on-site generation for a data center gets no fast track and still faces EFSB and local review. That is consistent with Neutral, but the Act does not address data-center loads directly.

btm_source.title: M.G.L. c.164, s.1B: Service territories for distribution companies
btm_source.shows: The distribution company has the exclusive obligation to provide distribution service in its territory, and no other person may provide distribution service there without the company's written consent. Generation supply is competitive.
btm_source.quote: no other person shall provide distribution service within such service territory without the written consent of such distribution company
btm_source.why: Distribution exclusivity limits third-party delivery over wires (e.g., off-site or co-located supply crossing to the load) unless the utility consents. Competitive generation supply and on-premises self-generation remain possible. That supports Restricted in part.

permitting_source.title: SDCL 49-41B-4 - Permit required before construction of facility after certain date
permitting_source.shows: Any 'facility' under the Energy Facility Siting Act (incl. an 'energy conversion facility' of 100 MW or more, per 49-41B-2) needs a Public Utilities Commission siting permit before construction.
permitting_source.quote: No utility may begin construction of a facility in the state on or after July 1, 1979, without first having obtained a permit issued with respect to such facility by the Public Utilities Commission
permitting_source.why: Shows a single state PUC siting permit for 100 MW+ thermal generation (one-stop, but a real state review); 49-41B-2 excludes 100 MW+ wind/solar from 'energy conversion facility'. Consistent with Permissive only in that it is a single, long-standing state process; it does not by itself show 'easy/streamlined'.

btm_source.title: SDCL 49-34A-42 - Electric utility's exclusive rights in assigned service area
btm_source.shows: Each electric utility holds the exclusive right to serve retail customers in its assigned service area; no other utility may serve there without written consent and PUC approval.
btm_source.quote: Each electric utility has the exclusive right to provide electric service at retail at each and every location
btm_source.why: Franchise exclusivity limits third-party retail sale to a large load (a Restricted-type feature), but SDCL 49-34A-56 lets new customers with a contracted minimum demand of 2,000 kW or more be released from the assigned utility after PUC notice and hearing, and owner-operated self-generation is not barred. Net: Permissive is defensible for large loads but the exclusivity rule should be noted; neither section addresses on-site generation directly.

large_load_tariff.name: New class for very large customers and data center rate schedule
large_load_tariff.quote: Petition for approval of a new class for very large customers generally, and a rate schedule for data center loads
large_load_tariff.note: Pending per SD PUC docket page (filed 07/27/26; staff data requests 10/07/26). Otter Tail is a small SD utility but the only SD large-load tariff filing found.

permitting_source.title: RSA 162-H:2 Definitions (Energy Facility Evaluation, Siting, Construction and Operation)
permitting_source.shows: Electric generating stations of 30 MW or more are 'energy facilities' needing a Site Evaluation Committee certificate.
permitting_source.quote: operation at any capacity of 30 megawatts or more
permitting_source.why: Shows a single state siting review for 30 MW+ generation (consistent with Neutral). That review is known to be demanding, so the rubric's 'heavy state siting review' could argue Restrictive. Nothing data-center-specific was found.

btm_source.title: RSA 362-A:2-a Purchase of Output of Limited Electrical Energy Producers by Persons Other Than Public Utilities
btm_source.shows: A limited electrical energy producer may sell to no more than 3 purchasers besides the franchise utility, and direct retail sales need PUC authorization and contract review.
btm_source.quote: not more than 3 purchasers other than the franchise electric utility
btm_source.why: Direct third-party retail sales are permitted only in limited form with Commission approval: consistent with Restricted. (A 2025 off-grid provider bill, HB 672, was not verified; the RSA site shows no codified off-grid chapter.)

permitting_source.title: ARC 9182C: Location and construction of electric power generating facilities, 199 IAC chapter 24 (Adopted and Filed)
permitting_source.shows: Rewritten generation-certificate rules (effective 2025-06-04). A state certificate is still required for major generation, but informational meetings are waived for wind, solar and storage projects that already hold their land rights, and the commission may waive chapter requirements.
permitting_source.quote: An applicant is not required to request or hold an informational meeting if
permitting_source.why: Shows a streamlined state generation-certificate process, which is consistent with Permissive. It is still a state siting review, and the rules do not address data-center load siting. Iowa Code pages (legis.iowa.gov) could not be reached (DNS failure).

btm_source.title: MidAmerican Energy Electric Tariff No. 2, Rider SPS: Standby and Supplementary Power Service (Sheet No. 478)
btm_source.publisher: MidAmerican Energy Company (tariff filed with the Iowa Utilities Board)
btm_source.shows: Standby and supplementary service is available to all nonresidential customers that have their own on-site parallel generation (required above 100 kW). It sets no size cap other than available utility capacity.
btm_source.quote: To all nonresidential customers in all systems of the Company's electric service area having their own generation facilities
btm_source.why: Customer-owned on-site generation of any size is accommodated by tariff, which fits Permissive. Third-party sales are not addressed here. (The Iowa Supreme Court's 2014 SZ Enterprises decision allowing an on-site third-party PPA is the stronger source, but no official copy could be retrieved.)

large_load_tariff.name: Rider ICR - Individual Customer Rate (new/expanding loads >=25 MW)
large_load_tariff.publisher: Interstate Power and Light (tariff filed with the Iowa Utilities Commission)
large_load_tariff.quote: The purpose of this Rider is to attract large incremental high load factor and highly flexible customer loads that provide net benefits to the Company's Iowa customers
large_load_tariff.note: Effective tariff sheet (Sub. Sixth Revised Sheet No. 80, effective 2024-10-01); written service agreement with minimum demand charges, filed with the Board 90 days before service; docket not shown on the sheet.

large_load_tariff.name: No large-load / data-center rate in Iowa Electric Tariff No. 2 (Rate ICR exists)
large_load_tariff.quote: RATE ICR, INDIVIDUAL CUSTOMER RATE AVAILABLE Service under this rate is available under written agreement for customers that meet the one of the two following conditions
large_load_tariff.note: Iowa tariff book (413 pp, checked 2026-10-14) has no large-load/data-center schedule; only the 2014 Rate ICR (negotiated, >=15 MW) and the pending-tariffs list (ia-pending-tariffs.pdf) shows no large-load filing. Judge whether ICR counts.

permitting_source.title: RSMo 144.810 Data storage centers, exemption from sales and use tax
permitting_source.shows: Missouri grants new and expanding data centers a sales/use tax exemption (up to 15 years) covering equipment and utilities, including electricity.
permitting_source.quote: Data storage centers, exemption from sales and use tax
permitting_source.why: Shows a pro-data-center state posture but is an incentive, not a siting/permitting rule. (SB 4 2025, RSMo 393.130.7, also requires large-load tariffs for 100 MW+/50 MW+ customers; the revisor page for it was not fetched.)

btm_source.title: RSMo 386.020 Definitions (subdivision 15, electrical corporation)
btm_source.shows: Generation on private property for the producer's own use or its tenants, not for sale to others, is outside the 'electrical corporation' definition; selling to others brings the seller under PSC regulation.
btm_source.quote: except where electricity is generated or distributed by the producer solely on or through private property
btm_source.why: Self-generation is clearly allowed, but third-party sale to a data center would make the seller an electrical corporation, which leans Restricted under the rubric's third-party-sale criterion. Not upgraded to 'contradicts' because no PSC ruling on third-party on-site sales was fetched.

large_load_tariff.name: Large Load Rate Plan / Large Load Customer Service (LLCS) under Service Classification 11(M)
large_load_tariff.quote: On November 24, 2025, the Commission issued its Order Regarding Ameren Missouri's Request for Approval of a Large Load Rate Plan
large_load_tariff.note: Compliance tariff JE-2026-0076 filed 2025-12-05 with 2026-01-04 effective date (Commission order of 2025-12-08 cited).

large_load_tariff.utility: Evergy Missouri Metro / Evergy Missouri West
large_load_tariff.name: Large Load Power Service (LLPS) Rate Plan and tariffs (100 MW+)
large_load_tariff.quote: Evergy is authorized to file LLPS schedules consistent with the LLPS Rate Plan
large_load_tariff.note: Report and Order issued 2025-11-13, effective 2025-12-13 (copy filed as Commission Exhibit 603 in ET-2025-0184); compliance sheets filed 2026-02.

permitting_source.title: Conn. Gen. Stat. ch. 277a (Public Utility Environmental Standards Act), ss. 16-50i, 16-50x
permitting_source.shows: Electric generating facilities (except small own-use cogeneration of 25 MW or less, renewables of 1 MW or less, and emergency generators) need a Connecticut Siting Council certificate. The Council has exclusive jurisdiction, preempting local zoning.
permitting_source.quote: the council shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the location and type of facilities
permitting_source.why: On-site generation for a data center faces state certificate review, but that review preempts local fights, and the data-center load itself is under ordinary local zoning. A mixed picture consistent with Neutral.

btm_source.title: OLR Bill Analysis, HB 5469 (2026): An Act Concerning Colocated Electric Suppliers and Large Electric Load Customers
btm_source.publisher: Connecticut General Assembly, Office of Legislative Research
btm_source.shows: Proposed PURA licensing for anyone supplying behind-the-meter or co-located power to a customer of 50 MW or more, with the load plus a reserve margin to be met from new generation. The bill was tabled for the House calendar on 2026-04-07 with no further action (not enacted).
btm_source.quote: sets licensure requirements for co-located electric suppliers who provide electricity to large load customers
btm_source.why: Shows the legislative direction toward regulating BTM and co-located supply, which fits Restricted, but it is not current law. Current-law limits on third-party sales (supplier licensing under ch. 283) were not pinned to a specific quotable section.

permitting_source.title: KRS 278.704: Merchant electric generating facility construction certificate, setback requirements
permitting_source.shows: Merchant generation needs a Siting Board construction certificate. The default setbacks are 1,000 ft from adjoining property for the stack or turbine and 2,000 ft from residential neighborhoods, schools, hospitals and nursing homes. The section was amended in 2026 (HB 677 / HB 869).
permitting_source.quote: No person shall commence to construct a merchant electric generating facility until that person has applied for and obtained a construction certificate for the facility from the board.
permitting_source.why: State siting review plus fixed setbacks add friction for merchant or co-located generation, which leans toward Neutral. Nothing here targets data-center loads, and the PSC has approved large-load rates (e.g., KU/LG&E Rate EHLF, Cases 2025-00113/00114) rather than restrictions.

btm_source.title: KRS 278.018: Right to serve certified territory
btm_source.shows: Each retail electric supplier has the exclusive right to serve all electric-consuming facilities in its certified territory. Under KRS 278.010(4), a "retail electric supplier" is any person engaged in furnishing retail electric service.
btm_source.quote: each retail electric supplier shall have the exclusive right to furnish retail electric service to all electric -consuming facilities located within its certified territory
btm_source.why: Statutory exclusive service territories cover any person furnishing retail service, so third-party BTM sales to a data center are barred. Only self-owned on-site generation remains. That is the Restricted posture, not Permissive.

large_load_tariff.name: Rate EHLF - Extremely High Load Factor Service
large_load_tariff.quote: Available only for new Customers: 1) with a contract capacity greater than 50 MVA, and 2) an expected average monthly load factor above 85%
large_load_tariff.note: Original Sheet No. 26, issued by authority of PSC order in Case 2025-00113 dated 2026-02-16; billing demand floor 80% of contract capacity; terms in filed Electric Service Agreements.

large_load_tariff.name: Rate EHLF - Extremely High Load Factor Service
large_load_tariff.quote: Issued by Authority of an Order of the Public Service Commission in Case No. 2025-00114 dated February 16, 2026
large_load_tariff.note: Same EHLF terms as KU (>50 MVA, >85% load factor).

large_load_tariff.name: Tariff I.G.S. (Industrial General Service) large-load provisions for >=150 MW
large_load_tariff.quote: the revised Tariff I.G.S. shall apply only to large-load customers adding 150 MW or more of incremental load
large_load_tariff.note: Approved with modifications; long-term contract, minimum billing demand and financial safeguards for new large loads.

permitting_source.title: LD 307 (HP 207), 132nd Legislature: An Act to Establish the Maine Data Center Coordination Council and Place a Temporary Limitation on Certain Data Centers - bill status
permitting_source.shows: The statewide data center moratorium bill (20 MW+ loads, to late 2027) passed both chambers but was vetoed; the House failed to override 72-65 on 2026-04-29 and the bill is dead.
permitting_source.quote: Placed in the Legislative Files. (DEAD)
permitting_source.why: The owner note 'Statewide moratorium passed 2026' is WRONG: no moratorium is law (veto sustained 2026-04-29; Governor's 2026-04-24 release says she 'supports a temporary moratorium' but wanted a Jay project exemption, and created a council by EO instead). Restrictive can still be argued (Legislature passed it; LD 713 bars DCs from state business tax incentives; LD 912 caps DC supply), but the stated basis must be corrected.

btm_source.title: LD 912 (SP 402), Public Law 2025 c. 85: An Act to Limit the Amount of Electricity That May Be Provided to Data Centers on a Certain Commercial or Industrial Site
btm_source.shows: Amends 35-A MRSA 102(20-B): on-site/abutting generators serving commercial or industrial consumers are not T&D utilities, but the legacy off-grid-site exception does not apply if more than 25% of the generator's nameplate serves data centers.
btm_source.quote: does not apply if more than 25% of the nameplate capacity of the entity is used to serve data centers
btm_source.why: Co-located supply to a data center is allowed only on-site/abutting, and the statute specifically caps data-center use of the off-grid exception: a targeted restriction, consistent with Restricted.

permitting_source.title: Minn. Stat. 216B.72 Qualified Large-Scale Data Center Fee
permitting_source.publisher: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
permitting_source.shows: The 2025 data center law (1Sp2025 c 12) imposes an annual $2M-$5M fee on qualified large-scale data centers by peak demand, alongside a separate very-large-customer class and water/environmental provisions.
permitting_source.quote: QUALIFIED LARGE-SCALE DATA CENTER FEE
permitting_source.why: Shows special data-center requirements (fees, new rate class) but not a moratorium or prohibitive siting; fits between Neutral and Restrictive. Neutral is defensible; the rubric's 'special DC requirements' would push toward Restrictive.

btm_source.title: Minn. Stat. 216B.40 Exclusive Service Right; Maps
btm_source.publisher: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
btm_source.shows: Each electric utility holds the exclusive right to serve every present and future retail customer in its assigned service area.
btm_source.quote: each electric utility shall have the exclusive right to provide electric service at retail
btm_source.why: Utility franchise exclusivity bars third-party retail supply to a data center; self-generation is not addressed. Consistent with Restricted.

large_load_tariff.name: Very large customer (data center) tariff / new customer class (new loads 100 MW+, or 20-100 MW system-intensive)
large_load_tariff.quote: The Commission defined very large customers for purposes of Xcel's tariffs as new loads sized 100 MW or greater.
large_load_tariff.note: PUC page states the Commission's decision; secondary sources date the vote 2026-05-15; written order date not confirmed.

large_load_tariff.name: Very large customer tariff (proposed)
large_load_tariff.quote: The Commission directed Minnesota Power to file an updated proposed tariff by July 15, 2026.
large_load_tariff.note: Pending; date is the deadline for the updated filing, actual filing not confirmed.

permitting_source.title: SB 2001, 2024 Second Extraordinary Session (data center projects under the Mississippi Major Economic Impact Act) - bill history
permitting_source.shows: Adds data processing facilities to MMEIA projects with tax exemptions and 'acceleration of certain public utility approval requirements'; Section 22 declares utility facilities to serve such projects in the public interest and lets the utility sign a large-customer supply agreement with no Commission approval required.
permitting_source.quote: TO PROVIDE FOR THE ACCELERATION OF CERTAIN PUBLIC UTILITY APPROVAL REQUIREMENTS
permitting_source.why: Statute fast-tracks utility and generation approvals for large data center projects. Note: the legislature site serves an incomplete TLS chain (fetched with certificate verification off); content is the official bill history, Approved by Governor 01/30.

btm_source.title: SB 2001 (2024 2nd Ext. Sess.), enrolled text: amended Miss. Code 77-3-14 and new Section 22
btm_source.shows: Amended 77-3-14(6) exempts own-use generation from PSC certification (report only); Section 22 has the public utility serve covered data center projects 'on an exclusive basis'.
btm_source.quote: primarily for that person's own use and not for the primary purpose of producing electricity
btm_source.why: Self-generation is easy (report only), supporting Permissive for owner-operated on-site plants; but third-party supply runs through the certificated utility, which provides service on an exclusive basis for these projects. Permissive holds only for self-owned generation.

large_load_tariff.quote: Commercial and Industrial Rate and Rider Schedules
large_load_tariff.note: Current C&I tariff index lists no large-load/data-center schedule (only Large General Service, HLF, ALGS, economic development riders); data centers served under special contracts.

large_load_tariff.quote: Large Business Development Rider (LBD)
large_load_tariff.note: Current pricing-and-rates index has no data-center/large-load schedule; LBD is a general economic development rider, not a large-load tariff.

permitting_source.title: Wis. Stat. 196.491 - Strategic energy assessment; electric generating facilities and transmission lines
permitting_source.shows: Construction of a 'facility' (incl. a large electric generating facility of 100 MW or more) requires a PSC certificate of public convenience and necessity; generation and associated transmission may be reviewed in a single proceeding.
permitting_source.quote: no person may commence the construction of a facility unless the person has applied for and received a certificate of public convenience and necessity
permitting_source.why: A centralized PSC CPCN process for 100 MW+ generation (combined generation + transmission application, local ordinances cannot block site testing per (2r)) is consistent with a predictable state path, but it is a full state review. It shows a structured state process, not 'easy/streamlined'. No data-center-specific moratorium found.

btm_source.title: Wis. Stat. 196.01(5) - Definition of 'Public utility'
btm_source.shows: Anyone owning or operating equipment to furnish power 'directly or indirectly to or for the public' is a public utility subject to PSC regulation.
btm_source.quote: for the production, transmission, delivery or furnishing of heat, light, water or power either directly or indirectly to or for the public
btm_source.why: This broad definition is the basis on which Wisconsin has treated third-party on-site electricity sales as public-utility service. That leans toward Restricted, not Permissive, for third-party BTM; owner-operated self-generation is not covered. Whether a sale to a single data center is 'to or for the public' is an interpretation question (PSC and courts), so verify before re-tiering.

large_load_tariff.name: Very Large Customer (VLC) and Bespoke Resources Tariffs
large_load_tariff.quote: The Commission extended the VLC tariff minimum initial term length to 15 years.
large_load_tariff.note: Approved with modifications at the 2026-04-24 open meeting (threshold lowered 500 MW to 100 MW; full-benefits model only); written final order posted later on ERF; Oracle sought judicial review (2026CV256).

btm_source.title: AS 42.05.711 Exemptions (Alaska Public Utilities Regulatory Act)
btm_source.shows: Independent generators are exempt from RCA regulation only when they sell solely to RCA-regulated utilities (renewables up to 65 MW), otherwise a seller of power needs RCA certification or a case-by-case public-interest exemption.
btm_source.quote: the electricity generated by the plant or facility is sold only to one or more electric utilities that are regulated by the commission
btm_source.why: Nothing bars a customer's own on-site generation, but there is no exemption for a third party selling directly to a large load; that seller would need an RCA certificate or a 42.05.711(d) exemption. That fits Permissive for self-owned generation and leans Restricted for third-party supply.

permitting_source.title: R.I. Gen. Laws 42-98-3, Energy Facility Siting Act definitions
permitting_source.shows: Generation facilities of 40 MW or more are 'major energy facilities' requiring Energy Facility Siting Board licensing.
permitting_source.quote: designed or capable of operating at a gross capacity of forty megawatts (40 MW) or more
permitting_source.why: State siting-board review for on-site or supply plants >=40 MW is a moderate hurdle, consistent with Neutral; no DC-specific moratorium found. Does not cover the data center load itself.

btm_source.title: R.I. Gen. Laws 39-1-2, Definitions (public utility)
btm_source.shows: The public-utility definition has no general exclusion for on-site or third-party electricity sales to a private customer; the only electricity carve-out is supply to a state-owned facility from an adjacent site.
btm_source.quote: Producing and/or distributing thermal energy and/or electricity to a state-owned facility
btm_source.why: A third party selling on-site power to a private data center would fall within the public-utility definition, so co-located third-party supply is restricted (self-generation for own use is not addressed). Consistent with Restricted.

permitting_source.title: 30 V.S.A. § 248 - New gas and electric purchases, investments, and facilities; certificate of public good
permitting_source.shows: No person may begin site preparation for or construction of any in-state generation, storage or transmission facility (at any voltage) without a Public Utility Commission certificate of public good, except facilities operated solely for on-site consumption by their owner.
permitting_source.quote: no person ... may begin site preparation for or construction of an electric generation facility
permitting_source.why: Comprehensive state CPG review of all grid-connected generation leans toward Restrictive for supply-side siting; owner-operated on-site generation is exempt. A 2026 AI data center moratorium bill (S.205) was introduced but stayed in Senate Finance (bill page checked). Neutral is defensible, but this is a heavier state review than most.

btm_source.title: 30 V.S.A. § 249 - Service territories; Commission jurisdiction
btm_source.shows: The Public Utility Commission establishes and alters exclusive service territories for distribution utilities.
btm_source.quote: jurisdiction to establish service territories for companies subject to its supervision that are engaged in the distribution of electrical energy
btm_source.why: Assigned service territories underpin a Restricted posture on third-party supply. However, § 248(a)(2) exempts generation 'operated solely for on-site electricity consumption by the owner' from the CPG, so owner-operated BTM is easier than third-party BTM. Supports Restricted for third-party arrangements only.

permitting_source.title: HCR 206 HD1 (2026): Requesting the Hawaii State Energy Office to convene a working group to study the potential impacts of large data centers
permitting_source.shows: The Legislature asks the State Energy Office to study data centers of 5 MW or more and to evaluate regulatory safeguards, citing the sensitivity of Hawaii's isolated island grids. It is a study request, not a siting rule or moratorium.
permitting_source.quote: Hawaii's isolated island electric grids are uniquely sensitive to large new electricity loads and require careful planning
permitting_source.why: Shows a cautious state posture toward large loads (and notes Hawaii has had no hyperscale proposals yet), but imposes no binding siting review or moratorium. Restrictive rests on grid constraints rather than a statute. A Hawaii County zoning bill (Bill 170) to bar data centers was reported but no county primary page was verified.

btm_source.title: Act 9, SLH 2011 (S.B. 704): amends HRS 269-1 definition of "public utility"
btm_source.shows: Exempts from public-utility regulation only third-party owners of RENEWABLE systems on the customer's property that sell to that customer or to the utility. A third party selling power from fossil on-site generation to a customer stays a regulated public utility.
btm_source.quote: Owns, controls, operates, or manages a renewable energy system that is located on a customer's property
btm_source.why: Third-party on-site supply is allowed only for renewables (and contiguous customer property). Non-renewable third-party BTM supply to a large load would make the seller a public utility. That fits Restricted.
